title: Nachshon Jumps In First
summary: The Israelites stand before the Red Sea, and no one dares to go into the water. Nachshon son of Amminadab walks in first, and the sea splits in two. Then Miriam drums and sings, and every morning manna falls from the sky. A story about the courage to be first.
pages:
The Israelites walked and walked in the desert, until they came to a great big sea.
It was called the Red Sea.

Behind them they heard the noise of horses and chariots.
Pharaoh had changed his mind, and wanted to bring them back to Egypt!
The sea in front, and Egypt behind. What should they do?

Everyone stood on the shore, afraid.
"You go in first," said one.
"No, you!" said another.
And nobody moved.

Only Nachshon son of Amminadab rolled up his sleeves.
"God told us to go forward," he said. "So I'm going."

Nachshon walked into the water.
The water came up to his knees, cold.
Then to his waist.
Then to his shoulders.

And the water came all the way up to his chin!
His heart pounded hard, but he did not turn back.

Moses raised his staff over the sea, and a strong wind blew all night long.
And the sea... split in two!
A wall of water on the right, and a wall of water on the left.

In the middle a path of dry land opened up.
Everyone crossed on it: fathers and mothers, grandpas and grandmas, children, babies, sheep and cows.

When everyone reached the other side, Moses and all the people sang a great song of thanks to God.
"I will sing to God, for He is greatly exalted!"

And Miriam took her drum, and went out dancing with all the women.
Boom-boom-tak! Boom-boom-tak!
The children danced and jumped too.

In the desert there was no food. But every morning manna fell from the sky:
little white flakes, sweet as cookies made with honey.
And on Friday a double portion of manna fell, so that on Shabbat no one would have to gather it, and everyone could rest.
